title: Text you type inside a component does not wear the screenshot halo
goal: Words typed on a screenshot get a soft white glow behind them so they stay readable over a photo. Inside a component that glow reads as a printing error: the label on a button you drew looks smudged. Text that sits inside a component should be drawn clean, the way the built in components already are.
notes: Found in the step E9 sitting on 2026-09-03. See the renders /tmp/photonz-playtest/component-end-to-end-walk/e2e-3-three-copies-doc.png: the word Save carries a visible light halo on every copy. StarterComponents.swift already strips the halo for the five built ins and says why; hand authored text keeps it. Decide whether the rule is per component or per group, and whether it is a stored property or a render time rule, since it must not bake into pixels.
acceptance: A text layer inside a component draws with no halo, on the original and on every copy
Text outside a component still keeps its halo over a screenshot
Grouping existing text into a component drops the halo, and ungrouping puts it back
A before and after picture is in the audit

log.note: Reproduced from the e2e walk render: black Save text on the red button carries a light halo on the original and on all three copies. Halo is layer.style.shadow, minted by TextBuilder.autoContrastShadow at creation and refreshed on recolor.

Adversarial review before building. (1) Per COMPONENT, not per group: grouping an arrow with its caption is the everyday redline move and that caption must keep its halo, so a plain group cannot carry the rule. Promoting to a component is a statement that this is a piece of UI. (2) The rule has to cover copies as well as the original, since a copy is a group carrying instanceOf, not componentID. (3) Render time, not stored: storing it would mean Make Component silently edits your text, and un-making it could not put back a halo it had already erased. (4) Suppress only the AUTOMATIC halo, not a shadow somebody chose: a title on a card is allowed to cast a shadow. (5) Shortest version that delivers it: one predicate in the model, one call site in the renderer, one binding in the inspector so the shadow switch stops claiming a halo that is not drawn. (6) Out of scope on purpose: a label typed straight onto a Frame still wears the halo. Filing that separately rather than widening this.

Built. Layer.drawnShadow(insideComponent:) is the whole rule, matched by value against TextBuilder.autoContrastShadow so only the AUTOMATIC halo steps aside. DocumentRenderer carries an insideComponent flag down compositeLayers/groupImage/ciImage and seeds it from document.isInsideComponent in renderSprite, so thumbnails and drag previews agree with the canvas. ShadowInspector now describes the drawn shadow, so the Enable Shadow switch reads off for a label inside a component instead of claiming a halo nobody can see. 12 core tests + 4 render tests written first; all 2076 green.

Verified in the probe app with Scripts/playtest/component-text-halo-walk.json. Loose text: halo. Grouped but not promoted: halo. Promoted: clean. Copy off the shelf: clean. Ungrouped again: halo back, nothing erased. A second walk picked the label inside the component and photographed the Shadow section: switch off, sliders gone, matching the canvas. Screen Recording was granted, so the audit ships three real captures.

Adversarial review of the built thing. It is invisible by design and there was nothing clumsy to fix in the flow. Two rough edges recorded in the audit rather than fixed: the difference is quiet at window size and reads best zoomed, and a halo somebody tuned by hand before promoting keeps drawing inside the component, which is deliberate but unexplained on screen. Text typed straight onto a Frame still wears the halo; filed as its own task (text-you-type-on-a-screen-does-not-wear-the-scre) rather than widening this one.
